CHAPTER XVII
OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
303. Theft.
(1) Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any moveable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
(2) Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment, or with fine, or with both.
Provided that the property is returned to its owner in the circumstances specified by this provision.
Explanation 1.— A thing attached to the earth is not moveable property.
Illustrations.
(a) A cuts down a tree on Z's ground with the intention of dishonestly taking the tree.
(b) A puts a bait for dogs in his pocket, and thus induces Z's dog to follow it.
304. Snatching.
(1) Theft is snatching when moveable property is suddenly or forcibly taken from a person.
For the reference-extraction fixture, see section 303.
